items.title: Net force and acceleration
items.stem: A 5.0 kg block rests on a frictionless horizontal surface. A 25 N force pulls it to the right and a 15 N force pulls it to the left. Find the magnitude and direction of the block's acceleration.

plain.learner_facing_text: Applies Newton's second law with the net force: a = (25 N − 15 N)/5.0 kg = 2.0 m/s².
States that the acceleration points to the right, toward the larger force.

latex.learner_facing_text:
Applies Newton's second law with the net force:
\[a=\frac{25\,\mathrm{N}-15\,\mathrm{N}}{5.0\,\mathrm{kg}}=2.0\,\mathrm{m/s^2}.\]
States that the acceleration points to the right, toward the larger force.

responses.correct: The net force is 25 N − 15 N = 10 N to the right. a = F/m = 10 N / 5.0 kg = 2.0 m/s², directed to the right.
responses.wrong: I add the forces: a = (25 N + 15 N)/5.0 kg = 8.0 m/s², directed to the right.
responses.vague: You use Newton's second law with the forces and the mass to get the acceleration.

items.title: Center of mass of two masses
items.stem: A 6.0 kg mass sits at x = 2.0 m and a 3.0 kg mass sits at x = 5.0 m on the same axis. Find the x-coordinate of the center of mass.

plain.learner_facing_text: Uses the weighted average of the positions: x_cm = (6.0 kg × 2.0 m + 3.0 kg × 5.0 m)/(6.0 kg + 3.0 kg) = 3.0 m.
Measures both positions from the same origin.

latex.learner_facing_text:
Uses the weighted average of the positions:
\[x_{\mathrm{cm}}=\frac{6.0\,\mathrm{kg}\times 2.0\,\mathrm{m}+3.0\,\mathrm{kg}\times 5.0\,\mathrm{m}}{6.0\,\mathrm{kg}+3.0\,\mathrm{kg}}=3.0\,\mathrm{m}.\]
Measures both positions from the same origin.

responses.correct: x_cm = (6.0 × 2.0 + 3.0 × 5.0)/(6.0 + 3.0) = 27/9 = 3.0 m, with both positions measured from the same origin.
responses.wrong: x_cm = (6.0 × 2.0 + 3.0 × 5.0)/2 = 13.5 m, because there are two masses.
responses.vague: Take the weighted average of the two positions.

items.title: Exact value of a reciprocal trig function

plain.learner_facing_text: Rewrites as a reciprocal of sine and evaluates: csc(5π/6) = 1/sin(5π/6) = 1/(1/2) = 2.
States the final value in simplest form.

latex.learner_facing_text:
Rewrites as a reciprocal of sine and evaluates:
\[\csc(5\pi/6)=\frac{1}{\sin(5\pi/6)}=\frac{1}{1/2}=2.\]
States the final value in simplest form.

responses.vague: Take the reciprocal of the sine of the angle.
